note: S73 canonical space state at an epoch boundary; fold-forward delta proofs, XOR null shown forgeable. Scaling rows are MEASURED POINTS, not a rate: units.check_affine refuses an affine fit.

controls.name: C_reader_roundtrip
controls.must_fire_because: any atom fails to round-trip, or the reader dropped an unbalanced form -- the atom set would not be the corpus
controls.can_fail_because: roundtrip_failures > 0 or dropped_forms > 0. Mishandling `;` inside a string literal, or `\"` inside one, produces exactly that.

controls.name: C_incremental_equals_full
controls.must_fire_because: a computed root differs from the rebuilt root in any epoch -- apply_insert would have a wrong case and the delta proof would be unsound
controls.can_fail_because: agreed < epochs. A wrong branch in apply_insert shows up here and nowhere else.

controls.name: C_apply_insert_cases
controls.must_fire_because: the branch-add (1) or mid-prefix fork (4) case is never reached, OR cases 2/3 fire while the encoding is still prefix-free, OR prefix_free goes False -- in which case cases 2 and 3 are live code that nothing here tests
controls.can_fail_because: case_1 or case_4 reads 0, i.e. the equality control never drove that branch at all.

controls.name: C_wrong_prior_root
controls.must_fire_because: a delta verifies against a prior root it was not built on -- epochs would not chain
controls.can_fail_because: verify_epoch_delta returns a root instead of None under the wrong genesis.

controls.name: C_smuggled_extra_atom
controls.must_fire_because: an undeclared atom leaves the computed root unchanged -- the delta would bound additions it does not name

controls.name: C_content_not_shape
controls.must_fire_because: two spaces of equal size with different atoms share a root -- this is S65, where 100% of leaves were "()" and the root was forged in 6 lines without running hyperon
controls.can_fail_because: root_a equals root_b while n_a == n_b. This is the S65 outcome.

controls.name: C_insertion_order_invariance
controls.must_fire_because: two insertion orders of one atom set give two roots -- replicas that learned the same facts in different orders would never agree

controls.name: C_sharing_real
controls.must_fire_because: the mean recomputed-node fraction reaches 0.5 -- structural sharing would buy nothing and an epoch would cost a rebuild
controls.can_fail_because: mean_fraction reaches 0.5 -- every epoch rehashing half the trie.

controls.name: C_xor_forgeable
controls.must_fire_because: no equal-digest different-space can be built -- XOR would be a sound set commitment and the trie would be unjustified
controls.can_fail_because: xor_base != xor_forged, i.e. no duplicate-atom collision exists and XOR is a sound set commitment after all.

controls.name: C_xor_cannot_prove_absence
controls.must_fire_because: the trie absence proof is not larger than the 32-byte XOR digest -- it would carry no structure the digest lacks
controls.can_fail_because: trie_absence_proof_bytes <= 32, i.e. the trie proof carries no structure the bare digest lacks.

controls.name: C_root_is_state_not_history
controls.must_fire_because: two epoch groupings of one atom set reach different roots -- then the root is not a state commitment. It also means the root does NOT bind history: binding that needs the chain of (root, delta) pairs hashed together, which this spike does not build
controls.can_fail_because: grouping_a != grouping_b, i.e. the root depends on how the atoms were batched into epochs.

falsifier: Exhibit an epoch delta this verifier folds to the prover's new root while the added atom set differs from the one it declares -- that refutes the delta proof. Or: show two epoch groupings of one atom set reaching different roots, which refutes it as a state commitment at all.
